args.text: [lane-marten] Risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to an old server after a site moves, causing outages or errors. (2) Slow failover: when a service switches to a backup, cached answers keep traffic going to the failed machine. (3) Security exposure: a forged or poisoned answer stays in the cache longer, so more people are misdirected for longer.

[lane-marten] Idempotent (safe to repeat) retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a sender often cannot tell whether its first request succeeded. If repeating the request gives the same result as doing it once, the sender can retry freely without causing duplicate payments, orders or messages.

[lane-marten] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (a universally unique identifier that starts with a timestamp) as a primary key: (1) Size: it takes 16 bytes, which is larger than a plain whole-number key, so indexes grow and use more memory. (2) Information leak: the timestamp is visible in the identifier, so outsiders can estimate when a record was created and roughly how fast new ones appear.

[lane-marten] A write-ahead log is a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data, so that after a crash it can replay or undo those changes and stay consistent. It also makes writes faster, because adding to the end of a log is quicker than updating many places in the main data at once.

[lane-marten] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed or behaviour by itself, so results from different runs would no longer be comparable. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the test with the same software and get the same kind of result, which makes any change in the numbers traceable to what you actually altered.
